  1000	def kv_pool_tokens(model: Model, topo: Topology) -> float:
  1001	    """KV-cache capacity of ONE cache (tokens), from the transparent memory model.
  1002	
  1003	    A replica group owns `topo.tp` GPUs. The weights are sharded across them and
  1004	    so are counted ONCE; the reserve is scratch space and is charged per GPU:
  1005	
  1006	        pool = tp*vram - weights - tp*reserve
  1007	
  1008	    This is per-GROUP, i.e. per-cache. A dp>1 deployment has topo.replicas of
  1009	    them, each independent — multiply for the system total, and only with
  1010	    session-sticky routing. Substituting tp=1 recovers the old single/DP-replica
  1011	    branch and tp=n the old TP branch, so every published number is unchanged.
  1012	
  1013	    A model too large for its group still clamps to 0 (the study's existing
  1014	    "does not fit" sentinel, asserted for GLM-5.3 on one GPU in _selfcheck).
  1015	    min_tp_for() reports the group size that would fit.
  1016	
  1017	    The activation reserve is the H200-calibrated ACT_RESERVE applied per GPU
  1018	    on every part, plus the part's reserve_extra — the measured H200 HBM
  1019	    over-provision the solved reserve implicitly absorbed, added back on parts
  1020	    that do not share it (see GPU.reserve_extra and docs/scenarios.md).
  1021	    A topology that carries a measured reserve (Topology.reserve, or the three
  1022	    terms in Topology.reserve_terms) uses it instead: per_gpu_reserve().
  1023	    """
  1024	    check_dtype_supported(model, topo)
  1025	    reserve = per_gpu_reserve(topo)
  1026	    # NOT factored as tp*(vram - reserve) - w: keeping the three terms in the
  1027	    # original order makes every pre-existing configuration bit-identical to the
  1028	    # pre-grid code (tp=1 reproduces the old single/DP branch, tp=n the old TP
  1029	    # branch) rather than merely equal after formatting.
  1030	    pool_bytes = topo.tp * topo.gpu.vram - hbm_weights(model) - topo.tp * reserve
  1031	    # ...in tokens of the cache the group STORES: a replicated layout pays
  1032	    # kv_bpt x copies per token (kv_replication), so the same bytes hold
  1033	    # fewer tokens. 1.0 on every default ("dcp") topology at a TP the KV
  1034	    # heads divide, i.e. every published number.
  1035	    return max(pool_bytes, 0.0) / _replicated(model, topo).kv_bpt

  1038	def effective_bw(topo: Topology) -> float:
  1039	    """Effective decode bandwidth seen by ONE replica group.
  1040	
  1041	    A group is `topo.tp` GPUs, so it sees tp x HBM less the TP haircut. DP adds
  1042	    groups, it never widens one — topo.replicas enters only in the aggregate
  1043	    (see decode_curves).
  1044	    """

897	def tp_efficiency(tp: int, nvlink_domain: int = 8) -> float:
   898	    """Aggregate-bandwidth efficiency of a TP group of `tp` GPUs.
   899	
   900	    ASSUMPTION: the baseline's 0.90 haircut is applied PER DOUBLING
   901	    (0.90^log2(tp)): TP2 -> 0.90 (the original assumption, unchanged),
   902	    TP4 -> 0.81, TP8 -> 0.73. Real efficiency depends on interconnect and
   903	    kernel overlap; treat >2 GPUs as a projection needing measurement.
   904	
   905	    Past `nvlink_domain` GPUs the group leaves the node's NVSwitch fabric and
   906	    each further doubling takes an additional CROSS_DOMAIN_EFFICIENCY penalty.
   907	    That second regime is UNMEASURED and deliberately pessimistic: its purpose
   908	    is to stop the in-node haircut being extrapolated to multi-node TP, where it
   909	    would badly overstate throughput. Both parts here are 8-GPU nodes, so every
   910	    configuration the study reports stays in the first regime.
   911	    """
   912	    if nvlink_domain < 1 or int(nvlink_domain) != nvlink_domain:
   913	        raise ValueError(
   914	            f"nvlink_domain must be a positive integer, got {nvlink_domain!r}")
   915	    if tp <= 1:
   916	        return 1.0
   917	    eff = TP_EFFICIENCY ** np.log2(min(tp, nvlink_domain))
   918	    if tp > nvlink_domain:
   919	        eff *= CROSS_DOMAIN_EFFICIENCY ** np.log2(tp / nvlink_domain)
   920	    return float(eff)
   921	
   922	
   923	def vllm_tp_refused(model: Model, tp: int) -> str | None:
   924	    """Why vLLM refuses TP width `tp` for `model`, or None when it accepts
   925	    it. Configs refuse such a width (RunConfig.validate) and the explorer does
   926	    not offer it: no vLLM deployment matches it."""
   927	    if not model.vllm_tp:
   928	        return (f"{model.name}: the TP sizes vLLM accepts are not recorded: "
   929	                f"set vllm_tp in catalog.toml (`ws catalog REPO` prints it)")
   930	    if tp in model.vllm_tp:
   931	        return None
   932	    sizes = ", ".join(map(str, model.vllm_tp))
   933	    return (f"vLLM refuses tensor_parallel {tp} for {model.name}; it accepts "
   934	            f"{sizes} (research/kv_tp_sharding.md #6)")

kv_pool_tokens (src/workingset/model.py) takes the HBM left after weights and the per-GPU reserve and divides it by the KV bytes per token; tp_efficiency scales effective bandwidth down once TP crosses the NVLink domain. I added the comment to tp_efficiency; the JS mirror in interactive/src needs no change because the comment does not alter behaviour.
